sources.title: Independent exact softmax, feature mixing and nullspace derivations
sources.details: For scores [1,0], Z=e^1+e^0=3.718281828459045; p=e/Z=0.7310585786300049 and 1-p=0.2689414213699951. Feature c is p*V0[c]+(1-p)*V1[c], giving [7.041644364930054,14.083288729860108,21.124933094790162]; V0 doubled gives [14.352230151230103,28.704460302460205,43.05669045369031]. Dimensions [Tq,Dk]@[Dk,Tk]→[Tq,Tk], row-softmax then @[Tk,Dv]→[Tq,Dv]. For any nonzero delta, replace V0 by V0+delta and V1 by V1-p/(1-p)*delta; the same weights cancel both changes, so the mixture does not uniquely determine all values. Numeric cards are dimensionless; softmax denominator is over the two candidates, not query rows or V features.

claims.statement: K supplies compatibility/matching information while paired V supplies numeric content; Q/K width may differ from V width.
claims.scope: Standard key-value attention roles; 2 matching features versus 3 returned features is allowed. Values are numeric learned representations in a model, not necessarily human-readable semantic content.

evidence.locator: §3.2 pp.3–4; §3.2.1 p.4 first paragraph and Eq.(1)
evidence.supports: Defines query and key-value mapping, assigns each value a weight from compatibility with its corresponding key, and names query/key dimension d_k separately from value dimension d_v.

claims.statement: This transparent example computes softmax(QKᵀ)V: match, normalize over candidates, then mix values, intentionally deferring scaling to 3.5.
claims.scope: Unscaled dot-product example only; does not claim the full scaled Transformer formula is unscaled. No causal mask or trained projection in this fence.

evidence.locator: §3.2.1 p.4 Eq.(1) and immediately following paragraph
evidence.supports: Eq.(1) establishes score→softmax→V pipeline; the following paragraph explicitly identifies dot-product attention as the same algorithm except for the scaling factor.
Normalization is per supplied dim; the final axis is the candidate axis in this score table.

claims.statement: For q=[1,0] and identity keys, scores are [1,0], weights round to [0.731,0.269], and output rounds to [7.042,14.083,21.125].
claims.scope: Values and outputs are dimensionless three-feature cards. The output is computed from full-precision softmax weights before rounding displayed values.

evidence.locator: Scalar formula and Z=e+1 derivation; probe-result.json denominator/weights_scalar/output_scalar
evidence.supports: Independently computes both weights with denominator over exactly two candidates and all three weighted features, not merely copying stdout.
Original float32 forward calculation prints the matching weights and output.
Checks original float32 against independent scalar values and checks higher precision plus published rounding.

verification.observed: Original float32 output [7.041644573212,14.083289146423,21.124935150146]; maximum absolute error 2.055356322472335e-6. All printed three-decimal output numbers match scalar rounding.
verification.tolerance: float32 absolute error <3e-6; float64 absolute error <=1e-12 with rtol=0; three-decimal rounding error <=0.0005. Displayed rounded weight multiplication is itself approximate: true p differs from displayed 0.731 by 0.00005857863, giving at most |V0[c]-V1[c]|*0.00005857863 output deviation (0.000644365,0.001288730,0.001933095).
verification.details: The literal rounded-coefficient first-feature calculation is 7.041; the text uses ≈ and previously marks coefficients approximate, while 7.042 is the correct rounding of the underlying softmax result. The stated approximations and error propagation agree; no exact equality is claimed for rounded coefficients.

claims.statement: torch.tensor builds the explicit 2D cards; k.T transposes the 2D keys; @ performs matching and value mixing; softmax(dim=-1) normalizes candidate columns; shape prints [1,3]. This fence only performs a forward demonstration.
claims.scope: Grouped API claim covers each API actually used. No trainable tensors, model, loss, backward, or parameter update in the original fence.

evidence.supports: tensor copies nested numeric data with default requires_grad=False; two 2D inputs give matrix-matrix product with matching inner dimensions.
T reverses the two axes of the lesson's 2D K; Tensor.softmax aliases functional.softmax.
softmax over dim=-1 rescales each query's candidate scores independently to sum to one.
Actual original code execution succeeds and records the [1,3] result, CPU device and dependency version.

claims.statement: Candidate key/value rows must preserve pairing; swapping only V assigns existing weights to different content and changes the answer.
claims.scope: Statement concerns swapping rows in the nonidentical toy values with nonuniform weights; simultaneous key/value reordering preserves the paired mapping.

evidence.supports: Each value weight comes from compatibility with the corresponding key, so K/V row pairing is essential.

evidence.supports: Only-V swap gives [1.9583556351,3.9167112701,5.8750669052], while jointly swapping K and V gives the original output exactly within 1e-12.

verification.details: Same fixed Q and same two source pairs; float64 on CPU with absolute tolerance 1e-12. Personally viewed both figure widths and checked left/right arrows and labels match row indices.

claims.statement: Self-attention forms Q, K and V from the same position-representation table X through distinct trainable Linear weights; this section instead fills Q/K/V directly.
claims.scope: Standard dense self-attention projection construction, supported by original method and repository contract. Trainability is not a claim that this fence executes projections or trains weights.

evidence.locator: §3.2.2 pp.4–5 learned W_i^Q/W_i^K/W_i^V; §3.2.3 p.5 self-attention bullet
evidence.supports: Separate learned projection parameter matrices transform queries/keys/values; self-attention obtains all three from the same previous-layer representations.
Linear transforms each final feature axis and allocates learnable weight Parameters.
Module weight Parameters are registered and default to requires_grad=True.
Distinct q/k/v nn.Linear modules apply to the same x and retain per-position representations.
A bounded untrained width-2 instance confirms three distinct parameter storages, each requires_grad=True, and all projections retain the [1,2,2] position table axes.

claims.statement: Doubling only the first V to [20,40,60] leaves Q/K-derived proportions unchanged and yields [14.352,28.704,43.057] after rounding.
claims.scope: Only V content changes; this is a role check under fixed unscaled scores, not evidence of learning quality.

evidence.supports: Independently recomputes all three features with original p and 1-p.
Executed the exact exercise as the small change, checked bit-equal weights and the three numerical outputs.

verification.observed: Float64 numerical assertions and exact weight equality pass; three-decimal rounding is [14.352,28.704,43.057].
verification.tolerance: Float64 absolute tolerance 1e-12, rtol=0; identical weights exact torch.equal; printed three-decimal rounding <=0.0005 per feature.
verification.details: Only first V row doubled; other value row, Q, K and denominator e+1 retained. All three features checked separately.

claims.statement: Weights [Tq,Tk] times V [Tk,Dv] returns [Tq,Dv], one Dv-wide result per query; matching width Dk need not equal Dv.
claims.scope: Two-dimensional unbatched transparent example and general matrix-shape rule; does not require Tq=Tk or Dk=Dv.

evidence.supports: Matrix multiplication contracts common candidate axis Tk while retaining query rows and value feature columns.
Separately names dk/dv and returns weighted combinations of dv-dimensional values.
Explicitly tracks which axes contract and which survive.
Original [1,3] and three-query/two-candidate [3,3] exercise validate unequal query/candidate counts and Dk=2,Dv=3; wrong-axis control detects query normalization.

verification.expected: Original Tq=1,Tk=2,Dk=2,Dv=3 returns [1,3]; bounded variant Tq=3,Tk=2 returns [3,3], each row's candidate weights sum to one.
verification.observed: Shapes exactly match. Three-query scores [3,2], output [3,3], row sums are one to 1e-12; wrong-axis sums are not one.
verification.tolerance: Shapes exact equality; row-sum absolute tolerance 1e-12 with rtol=0.
verification.details: The contracted output axis is Tk, not Dk or Dv. Output feature width comes from V; query count comes from Q. Entries are dimensionless cards, with no physical-unit conversion.

claims.statement: Mixing several values into one result generally cannot reconstruct all original values; a later residual route retains the incoming representation alongside attention.
claims.scope: Non-uniqueness of recovering values from one weighted result, even when the weights are known. It does not assert impossibility in every constrained case, or that the residual route reconstructs every source V.

evidence.locator: §3.2 pp.3–4 weighted sum; §3.2.2 p.5 averaging limitation; §3.1 p.3 residual LayerNorm(x+Sublayer(x))
evidence.supports: The attention result is a weighted sum and the authors describe limitations of averaging; original Transformer preserves an x residual route around the attention sublayer.
For positive two-candidate weights this yields distinct source values with exactly the same weighted mixture, establishing the stated general information-loss limitation.
Actual distinct two-row values [11,22,33] and [-3.7182818285,-7.4365636569,-11.1548454854] return the same result; measured max difference zero.
The later implemented block retains x through x=x+attended, consistent with the preview without asserting this toy fence includes that route.

factual_accuracy.details: All nine substantive groups checked: V/K roles, distinct widths, unscaled pipeline, base numbers, all actual APIs, paired row order, same-X trainable projections versus manually filled demonstration, exact exercise, general axes and information/residual preview. Mature-method properties follow the original paper, not conclusions inferred from toy tests.

limitations.details: Forward-only hand-filled example; no projection construction, gradient computation or parameter update in original code. Bounded probe separately checks projections' trainability but performs no backward/training. Unscaled scores are explicit and 3.5 supplies scaling; no causal restriction or quality/semantic claim made. Numeric labels are rounded; mixing limitation is generic rather than universal and residual preview does not imply recoverability. No datasets/models downloaded, no GPU, uploads, paid computation, full training or commits. Existing CPU environment needed no setup/configuration changes.
